newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia to cut civil service by 40 pct in two years.
newsitem.headline: Zambia to cut civil service by 40 pct in two years.

text.p: Zambia plans to cut its public service by 40 percent over the next two years, Vice President Godfrey Miyanda said.
Up to 11,000 members of the over 28,000-strong bureaucracy would be laid off by 1999, starting with over 3,400 workers this year, he told parliament on Wednesday.
"About 11,000 posts will go," he said, adding that job cuts would start in the ministries of finance, agriculture, commerce and in the public service management division.
Zambia's population is around nine million.
Finance Minister Ronald Penza said in his 1997/98 budget speech in January that some civil servants would receive government houses as part of severance packages.
